audit_findings.title: Current debt service is not represented in the FY2025 owner-earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.953 million difference between June 2026 total debt of $201.971 million and FY2025 year-end term-loan plus revolver borrowings of $149.018 million; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE valuation that does not deduct debt principal, normalized interest expense must be included in OE. A persistent increase in debt would reduce OE through after-tax interest, while lower rates or temporary seasonal borrowing could have the opposite effect.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025 , the Company had outstanding borrowings under the term loan of $ 144,018 , $ 5,000 in outstanding borrowings on the revolving credit facility and remaining borrowing availability of $ 119,450 .
audit_findings.explanation: The balance mismatch is demonstrated, but an overstatement is not. Six-month 2026 net interest expense was $4.386 million, below $5.357 million in the comparable 2025 period despite the June debt balance, so the filing does not establish that FY2025 interest understates the current sustainable charge. The June revolver balance may also be seasonal working-capital financing. Current-rate, swap and borrowing-duration information is insufficient to establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every component of the $201.971 million balance, determine the normalized post-season revolver balance, and rerun all scenarios using annualized after-tax interest under the $75 million swap and applicable rates on remaining debt.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only two months of the acquired Venco Venturo perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.254 million acquisition consideration; $2.763 million of two-month revenue and $0.083 million pre-tax operating loss; full-year OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A pro forma contribution would alter anchor OE through operating profit, maintenance capex, working capital, leases and acquisition financing rather than through the valuation bridge alone.
audit_findings.evidence: From the date of acquisition through December 31, 2025, the Venco Venturo assets contributed $ 2,763 of revenues and $ 83 of pre-tax operating loss.
audit_findings.explanation: The incomplete perimeter is demonstrated: FY2025 contains results only from November 3 onward, while current shareholders own the full business. The filing says the acquired operations represented less than 1% of 2025 consolidated sales and the $27.254 million purchase price equals about 3.9% of the $692 million base equity value, but neither measure establishes the acquired business's sustainable OE. Its direction is unresolved because the reported stub period lost money while integration and full-year economics are unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a filed-number reconciliation of Venco's first-half 2026 revenue, operating profit, working-capital investment, capex, leases and financing; insert its pro forma full-year OE into the anchor and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Actual capex may be below sustainable maintenance requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capex of $11.133 million versus the filed normal 2%-3% of $656.053 million sales, implying a $1.988-$8.549 million shortfall, equal to 3.8%-16.5% of the $51.9 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalizing maintenance capex reduces anchor OE dollar-for-dollar and therefore reduces forecast OE, operating PV, equity value per share and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, although modest, our annual capital expenditure requirements, which are normally budgeted around 2-3% of net sales, can be temporarily reduced by up to approximately 40% in response to actual or anticipated decreases in sales volumes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization gap if the anchor deducted only actual FY2025 capex. Management expressly says normal requirements are 2%-3% of sales and can be temporarily reduced. The implied adjustment reaches 16.5% of anchor OE, a scale reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation output even though its direction would reinforce, rather than reverse, the current price-above-value conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance, growth, acquired-business and deferred projects in FY2025 and 2026 capex; rerun all scenarios with a supported normalized maintenance charge within the filed $13.121-$19.682 million range.

audit_findings.title: The current lease burden is larger than the burden underlying the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Lease liability increased $22.519 million; six-month lease expense increased $1.295 million year over year, or $2.590 million annualized, equal to 5.0% of anchor OE before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Because lease liabilities are context-only, incremental recurring rent must reduce OE rather than be deducted again in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The lease agreement has an initial term of 15 years, with two optional 10 -year renewal options.
audit_findings.explanation: The larger lease perimeter is demonstrated, but the filed expense comparison limits its apparent scale. Annualizing the $1.295 million first-half expense increase gives $2.590 million before tax, about 5.0% of the $51.9 million anchor; after tax it would be smaller. The entire $22.519 million liability increase is only 3.3% of the $692 million base equity value and cannot properly be treated as an additional full bridge deduction when rent is expensed. On the supplied numbers, this is not large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $28.175 million of new right-of-use assets to facilities and escalation schedules, isolate their recurring annual rent, and confirm that amount in forecast OE without also deducting the lease liability.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition and refinancing one-offs may remain in the latest anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.853 million pre-tax: $1.521 million acquisition expense, $0.176 million debt-modification expense and $0.156 million extinguishment loss; approximately $1.413 million after the filed 23.75% tax rate, or 2.7% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing genuinely nonrecurring charges increases normalized anchor OE and all scenario values; retaining recurring deal costs leaves OE unchanged.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company incurred $ 1,521 of transaction expenses related to this acquisition that are included in selling, general and administrative expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income in the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges and their inclusion in FY2025 GAAP earnings are demonstrated, although their proper recurrence classification remains a judgment. Even if all three are removed, the computed after-tax adjustment is about $1.413 million, only 2.7% of the $51.9 million anchor. That scale is insufficient to change the valuation conclusion relative to the $42.30 market price and $32.73 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the three charges through the OE worksheet, document acquisition and refinancing frequency over the historical period, and apply a consistent recurring-cost policy; rerun only if additional omitted one-offs raise the total materially.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree benefits may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.390 million total postretirement obligation, including $4.190 million noncurrent and $0.200 million current; $0.728 million difference between the $0.455 million benefit credit and $0.273 million cash benefits paid
audit_findings.mechanism: The obligation could reduce the equity bridge, or a normalized cash benefit charge could reduce OE; applying both would double count the same claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Postretirement benefits of $ 4,190 and $ 3,319 as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 , respectively, are included in Retiree benefits and deferred compensation in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation and benefit credit are demonstrated. A full $4.390 million bridge deduction is only 0.6% of the $692 million base equity value, or approximately $0.19 per diluted share. Alternatively, replacing the credit with cash benefits changes pre-tax earnings by $0.728 million, only 1.4% of anchor OE before tax. Either treatment is too small to change the valuation conclusion, and the two treatments must not be combined.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile projected benefit payments, service cost and the actuarial-gain amortization to OE; select either a normalized cash charge or a bridge deduction and confirm no double counting.
